title: Cache writes from the flat total, the breakdown, or both, with absent, null, zero and invalid values
matrix: input, output, cache-read and cache-write breakdowns
policy: P8: the breakdown is used when the flat total is absent, null or invalid; an absent tier is 0. A flat total with no breakdown (absent, null or {}) is 5-minute writes. When both are valid, P9 applies unchanged: the breakdown if it adds up to the flat total, else the flat total as 5-minute writes; an invalid tier is read as 0 for that comparison. Invalid values flag the message. P9 mismatches of valid values are F11's.
derivation: Each record [1, 1]. a flat 40 -> 5m 40. b breakdown only -> 5m 200, 1h 100. c 1h only -> 1h 50. d 30 = 10 + 20 -> 5m 10, 1h 20. e flat null -> 5m 7, 1h 3. f flat "300" invalid -> 5m 60, 1h 40, flawed. g flat -5 invalid -> 5m 4, flawed. h 5m "x" read as 0: 0 + 25 = 25 -> 1h 25, flawed. i 5m -1 read as 0: 0 + 5 != 25 -> 5m 25, flawed. j breakdown null -> 5m 9. k breakdown {} adds to 0 != 12 -> 5m 12. l explicit 0 -> nothing. m all zeros -> nothing. 5m 40+200+10+7+60+4+25+9+12 = 367; 1h 100+50+20+3+40+25 = 238. 13+13+367+238 = 631. Flawed: f g h i = 4. Today b, c and e lose their breakdown (flat absent or null reads as 0, which they don't add up to), g subtracts 5 and f's "300" reads as 0.
